items.question: What basis enables the best of Raghus to perform all ritual acts?
premises: The mātṛkā letters serve as the foundation
Resorting to them precedes ritual action
All acts are to be performed on this basis
items.inference: By taking refuge in the mātṛkā letters, the practitioner can accomplish all prescribed rites.
items.plain_english: Having resorted to the letters of Mātṛkā, the best of the Raghus should perform everything.

items.question: According to what prior authority should the wise practitioner perform all acts?
premises: A tantra was previously spoken
Its method serves as the model
The wise practitioner follows that model
items.inference: The wise one should perform all acts in accordance with the previously taught tantra.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the wise one should perform everything just as in the previously spoken tantra.

rows.grounds: compound: sādhaka+yatna with ablative sense of manner

items.question: What practice must the practitioner undertake after the preceding steps?
premises: The sequence continues after prior acts
Recitation of mātṛkā is prescribed
It must be done with diligent effort
items.inference: The practitioner should next perform recitation of mātṛkā with earnest effort.
items.plain_english: Then the practitioner should diligently perform the recitation of Mātṛkā.

rows.grounds: compound: mātṛkā+dhyāna; object implied with kuryāt

items.question: Which ritual steps follow recitation in the prescribed sequence?
premises: Recitation has already been performed
Meditation on mātṛkā comes next
External placement follows after that
items.inference: After recitation, one should perform meditation on mātṛkā and then the external placement.
uncertainties: The governing verb kuryāt/ācaret is implied from context.
items.plain_english: Then indeed comes meditation on Mātṛkā, and after that the external placement.

items.question: How should the complete mātṛkā placement be characterized and performed?
premises: The preceding steps form a sequence
The placement is eightfold in nature
It is to be performed as prescribed
items.inference: One should thus perform the eightfold placement of mātṛkā.
items.plain_english: Thus, O Goddess, one should perform the eightfold placement of Mātṛkā.

rows.grounds: compound: guru+rūpaka; predicate describing the placement

items.question: What essential form does the excellent placement embody for the practitioner?
premises: The placement is described as excellent
It is characterized as having a guru-form
This is addressed to the supreme goddess
items.inference: The excellent placement embodies the form of the guru.
uncertainties: The copula is implied rather than expressed.
items.plain_english: O Supreme Goddess, the excellent placement has the form of the guru.

items.question: What new instruction is the speaker about to reveal to the goddess?
premises: The speaker announces a forthcoming teaching
The teaching concerns the placement of the three qualities
The listener is urged to attend carefully
items.inference: The speaker will now explain the placement of the three qualities.
items.plain_english: O Great Goddess, I shall tell you the placement of the three qualities; listen well.

rows.grounds: compound: bindu+ardha+candra+saṃyuta; sandhi within fused token

items.question: What divine and symbolic elements constitute the described form?
premises: The form is joined with Śiva, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā
It is joined with bindu and the half-moon
These elements define its composition
items.inference: The described form unites the triad of deities with bindu and the half-moon.
uncertainties: The noun qualified by these adjectives is supplied by the following verse.
items.plain_english: It is endowed with Śiva, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā, and joined with bindu and the half-moon.

rows.grounds: compound: sarva+upari; locative sense of position

items.question: What is the supreme nature of the bindu placed above all?
premises: The bindu is located above all
It is described as having the nature of Brahman
This is declared to the great goddess
items.inference: The supreme bindu is of the very nature of Brahman.
uncertainties: Case agreement between bindu and brahmasvarūpiṇam is irregular in the transmitted text.
items.plain_english: Above all, O Great Goddess, the bindu is of the nature of Brahman.

items.question: Where must the three-quality placement be ritually performed?
premises: The placement involves the three qualities
The locus is the place of the fifty mātṛkā letters
This placement is prescribed
items.inference: The three-quality placement should be performed in the locus of the fifty mātṛkā letters.
items.plain_english: One should perform the three-quality placement in the place of the fifty Mātṛkā letters.

rows.grounds: genitive specifying what has a secret

items.question: How is the hidden significance of this placement characterized?
premises: The placement possesses a secret
That secret is supremely wondrous
This is revealed to the supreme goddess
items.inference: The secret of this placement is supremely wondrous.
items.plain_english: O Supreme Goddess, the secret of this placement is supremely wondrous.

rows.grounds: past participle; sandhi form with following ca
ablative of cause or manner from vartana

items.question: By what process does the placement become threefold in application?
premises: The placement undergoes a process of turning
This turning occurs in a threefold manner
The result is a threefold state
items.inference: Through threefold turning, the placement becomes threefold.
uncertainties: The exact referent of gatañ is contextually compressed.
items.plain_english: And, O Supreme Goddess, by turning threefold it becomes threefold.

items.question: How many times must the three-quality placement be applied when divided?
premises: The placement can be applied in a divided form
The count reaches one hundred and eight
The three-quality placement is to be performed
items.inference: In its divided form, the three-quality placement should be performed one hundred and eight times.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, in the divided form one should place the three-quality placement one hundred and eight times.

items.question: What qualification is attained through performing only the three-quality placement?
premises: The three-quality placement alone is performed
This act confers a status
Tradition declares that status explicitly
items.inference: By merely performing the three-quality placement, one is declared qualified.
uncertainties: The specific domain of qualification is not explicitly stated.
items.plain_english: By the mere performance of the three-quality placement, one is said to be qualified.

rows.grounds: object; sandhi form with following ca

items.question: Where are diverse forms of placement taught in the tradition?
premises: Placements exist in various forms
Different tantras teach them
This diversity is traditionally acknowledged
items.inference: Various kinds of placement are taught in different tantras.
items.plain_english: And, O Goddess, various kinds of placement are taught in different tantras.

items.question: Which placement holds supreme power among all placements?
premises: Many placements exist
Mātṛkā is singled out among them
It is described as bewitching the world
items.inference: Among all placements, mātṛkā is the world-bewitching one.
items.plain_english: O Supreme Goddess, among all placements, Mātṛkā is the one that enchants the world.

items.question: Why must the practitioner perform the mātṛkā placement with special diligence?
premises: Mātṛkā is supreme among placements
This supremacy demands careful practice
The placement is therefore prescribed with effort
items.inference: Because mātṛkā is supreme, one should perform its placement with diligent effort.
items.plain_english: Therefore, O Goddess, one should indeed perform the placement of Mātṛkā with diligent effort.

rows.grounds: compound: mokṣa+pradāyinī; predicate describing ṣoḍhā mātṛkā

items.question: What further form of mātṛkā is introduced as granting liberation?
premises: The teaching moves beyond the previous topic

This sixfold form grants liberation
items.inference: Beyond this, the sixfold form of mātṛkā is declared to grant liberation.
items.plain_english: Beyond this, the sixfold form of Mātṛkā is the giver of liberation.

rows.grounds: subject or topic of the condition

items.question: Under what condition does the sixfold mātṛkā become fruitless for a practitioner?
premises: The sixfold mātṛkā is powerful in itself
For a certain practitioner it yields no result
Mātṛkā becomes fruitless in that case
items.inference: For such a person, the sixfold mātṛkā becomes fruitless.
uncertainties: The specific condition making it fruitless is implied rather than stated.
items.plain_english: And for him the sixfold practice is fruitless; Mātṛkā becomes fruitless.

items.question: What contrast distinguishes fruitful practice from futile effort?
premises: For the qualified practitioner results are always fruitful
Otherwise the effort yields no benefit
Futile effort is likened to crying in a forest
items.inference: When properly undertaken it is always fruitful, but otherwise it is like crying in the forest.
uncertainties: The subject of saphalāni is implied from the preceding context.
items.plain_english: For him they are always fruitful; otherwise it is like crying in the forest.

items.question: What is the ultimate ontological nature of the sixfold mātṛkā?
premises: The sixfold form is under discussion
It is identified directly with Brahman’s nature
This identity is affirmed emphatically
items.inference: The sixfold mātṛkā is directly of the nature of Brahman.
items.plain_english: Indeed, O Supreme Goddess, the sixfold form is directly of the nature of Brahman.

rows.grounds: compound: brahma+viṣṇu+nuta; describes the sixfold form
compound: sampuṭa+saṃsthita; locative sense within enclosure

items.plain_english: Praised by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, delightful, and situated within my enclosure.

items.question: How should the listener receive the teaching on the sixfold mātṛkā?
premises: The sixfold mātṛkā is being taught
The listener is addressed directly
Careful attention is required for comprehension
items.inference: The listener should attentively comprehend the sixfold mātṛkā.
items.plain_english: O fair-hipped one, comprehend the sixfold Mātṛkā with full attention.

premises: The fifty mātṛkā letters are the object
They are to be enclosed within the three qualities

items.inference: One should enclose the fifty mātṛkā letters within the three qualities.
uncertainties: The main verb governing the sequence is implied from the surrounding context.
items.plain_english: O beloved, having enclosed the fifty Mātṛkā letters within the three qualities.
